Let gravity have a say.

What this test shows

Assumed prototype

A model we can change.

  • 14 actuated axes: six per leg, plus phone pan and tilt.
  • 250 g phone, approximately 1.691 kg total mass. Total includes a 1 g screen proxy.
  • 80 mm thigh and shin links; 96 × 60 mm soles, 106 mm foot-centre spacing. About 370 mm overall height.
  • Leg torques limited to ±1.5 Nm; neck torques to ±0.25 Nm. Ideal position servos with damping; no measured motor model.
  • Gravity 9.81 m/s²; nominal sliding friction coefficient 0.8; 2 ms physics timestep; six seconds per test.

These stepping runs remain upright for the six-second window. Extra movement on the slippery floor can include sliding; distance alone is not a walking-quality score. Peak torque is a simulation observation, not a motor recommendation.

At nominal friction, exactly one sole contacts the floor in approximately 12% of sampled frames. Much of this early gait keeps both feet in contact.

Checks performed

Physics, with practical limits.

The standing ground reaction averages 16.589 N, matching model weight. Torque limits hold. Reducing the timestep from 2 ms to 1 ms changes stepping distance from 9.78 cm to 9.39 cm (4.0%).

Fall detection: body tilt exceeds 45° or pelvis height drops below 100 mm. The push is a 12 N horizontal force at the pelvis centre of mass for 160 ms, starting at t = 2 s.

This is a useful first dynamics experiment, with short test durations and simplified geometry. It does not establish robust balance or a production-ready gait.

Next engineering pass

From a shuffle to reliable walking.

  • Replace estimated masses, inertias and joint locations with CAD and measured phone properties.
  • Add IMU and foot-load feedback, body-weight transfer, foot trajectory planning and push recovery.
  • Model backlash, torque–speed curves, power limits, thermal behaviour and delays.
  • Enable robot self-collision after refining link collision geometry. This first model checks robot–floor collisions only.
  • Test turning steps, target tracking, obstacles, floor edges and a wider range of surfaces. Those behaviours are not yet simulated.
Reproduce or modify the physics with the included simulation script and MuJoCo model. Read the run summaries and numerical checks. Engine: MuJoCo. The animation is generated from simulated body positions; no root trajectory is imposed.
